derived.claim: Correction of my own F44: it holds for the global install only. In per-project mode (CLAUDE_HOME=$PWD/.claude, install.sh:21-22) AGENTS_DST is $PWD/.claude/agents (install.sh:36), the same path as a project-level copy. Outcomes for a copy of a shipped name: if the installer wrote that file earlier and the user edited it, the hash differs from the recorded one and the file is 'differs, kept' (install.sh:134-158). If the file was never installed, it is 'skip'. If the user passes --force (FORCE=1), the elif at ~line 97 runs cp -f and replaces the retuned copy with the shipped file, silently losing the edits. Uninstall removes recorded paths only when the hash matches (uninstall.sh:41-49), so it is safe. The recipe should say one thing: in a per-project install, edit the installed file in place, because a re-run keeps edits and only --force destroys them. Back up a copy before --force.

Uninstall refuses paths outside CLAUDE_HOME and removes only recorded paths.
